name.text: Would like create randomised stack statistics

questiontext.text:
The stacked dot plot below shows August precipitation (mm) for {@N@} observations from Eastern African cities (for example Nairobi, Addis Ababa, Kampala and Dar es Salaam). Each dot is one observation, placed at the centre of its 6 mm wide bin.

Drag the two vertical lines by their handles on the lower axis. Place the line labelled "Mean" where you estimate the mean, and the line labelled "Median" where you estimate the median.

[[jsxgraph input-ref-ans1="ref_M" input-ref-ans2="ref_D" width="640px" height="420px"]] var cnt = {#cnt#}; var nb = {#nb#}; var ymax = {#maxc#} + 2; var xmax = 6*nb; var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox:[-4, ymax, xmax+4, -3.5], axis:false, showCopyright:false, showNavigation:false}); board.create('axis', [[0,0],[1,0]], {ticks:{ticksDistance:6, minorTicks:0, insertTicks:false, drawLabels:true}}); board.create('text', [xmax/2-10, -3, 'August precipitation (mm)'], {fixed:true}); for (var i = 0; i < cnt.length; i++) { for (var k = 0; k < cnt[i]; k++) { board.create('point', [6*i+3, 0.5+k], {size:2, fixed:true, withLabel:false, name:'', color:'#444444', highlight:false}); } } var lineM = board.create('line', [[-100,-1],[100,-1]], {visible:false}); var lineD = board.create('line', [[-100,-2],[100,-2]], {visible:false}); var pM = board.create('glider', [xmax/2, -1, lineM], {name:'Mean', size:6, color:'red', label:{offset:[8,8]}}); var pD = board.create('glider', [xmax/2, -2, lineD], {name:'Median', size:6, color:'blue', label:{offset:[8,-14]}}); board.create('line', [[function(){return pM.X();}, 0],[function(){return pM.X();}, 1]], {straightFirst:false, straightLast:true, strokeColor:'red', strokeWidth:2, fixed:true, highlight:false}); board.create('line', [[function(){return pD.X();}, 0],[function(){return pD.X();}, 1]], {straightFirst:false, straightLast:true, strokeColor:'blue', strokeWidth:2, dash:2, fixed:true, highlight:false}); stack_jxg.bind_point(ref_M, pM); stack_jxg.bind_point(ref_D, pD); [[/jsxgraph]]
[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]]

Move both lines, then check. Marks: one third for the mean, one third for the median, one third for placing the mean line to the right of the median line.

[[feedback:prt_ans1]]

generalfeedback.text:
The mean is the sum of all dot positions divided by {@N@}, which gives {@tmd@} mm. The median is the middle value of the {@N@} ordered dots, which is {@medd@} mm.

There are {@nl@} dots below the median, {@nr@} dots above it and {@ne@} dots at it, so the median splits the dots into two nearly equal halves.

The distribution is right-skewed: most dots are in the low bins and a long tail stretches to the right. The median only depends on how many dots lie on each side, so the tail dots count no more than any other dot above the median. The mean uses the actual values, so the large values in the tail pull it towards the right. Hence the mean ({@tmd@} mm) is above the median ({@medd@} mm). This is typical of right-skewed data.

truefeedback.text: Mean: your line is within 10% of the true mean ({@tmd@} mm). Good.
Mean: within 20% of the true mean ({@tmd@} mm), but not within 10%. Think of the mean as the balance point of the dots: the long right tail pulls it to the right.

falsefeedback.text: Mean: more than 20% from the true mean ({@tmd@} mm). Think of the mean as the balance point of the dots: the long right tail pulls it to the right.

truefeedback.text: Median: your line is within 10% of the true median ({@medd@} mm). Good.
Median: within 20% of the true median ({@medd@} mm), but not within 10%. The median line should split the dots into two equal halves.

falsefeedback.text: Median: more than 20% from the true median ({@medd@} mm). The median line should split the dots into two equal halves.

node.description: Mean line right of median line

truefeedback.text: Position: the mean line is to the right of the median line.

falsefeedback.text: Position: the mean line is not to the right of the median line.
